narrative_summary: A pervasive tension between entrenched institutional power and disruptive forces defines the current political and technological landscape, stretching from electoral upsets and policy debates to geopolitical conflict. Domestically, insurgent progressive primary victories and contentious Senate races highlight a grassroots backlash against traditional political norms, while fiscal debates spotlight the long-term impacts of past tax policies. Internationally, strategic vulnerabilities in global shipping and energy infrastructure—exacerbated by ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine—reveal the fragile nature of economic stability and maritime access. Simultaneously, technological advancements in manufactured intelligence demonstrate both the promise of autonomous systems and the persistent vulnerabilities of group decision-making. Across all fronts, policymakers and analysts grapple with how to navigate systemic disruptions driven by economic pressure, political polarization, and rapid innovation.

source_summaries.title: Little-Known Episode Offers a Big Clue to El-Sayed’s Politics
bullets: Abdul El-Sayed's stance on health care remains a central issue in the Michigan Senate race due to his prominent advocacy for Medicare for All.
While he generally rejects incremental reforms, El-Sayed has expressed support for intermediate steps that reduce corporate power and expand public coverage.
El-Sayed lacks a legislative voting record from his time as a public health director, leaving voters to examine past episodes for clues on how he would legislate.

source_summaries.title: Announcing the Brussels Strategy Seminar — September 9
bullets: Prof Robert Pape and Aaron Maté are hosting an in-person Brussels Strategy Seminar at the European Parliament on September 9.
The panel discussion will examine the connection between the Iran war, the rise of violent populism in the United States, and their strategic implications for Europe.
A limited number of seats for the event are being made available to Substack subscribers through a registration process.

source_summaries.title: Azeem Azhar, Garry Kasparov, and Timothy Snyder posted new notes
bullets: Azeem Azhar published a new note on Substack regarding manufactured intelligence.
Garry Kasparov shared a note discussing the Republican Party.
Timothy Snyder posted a note concerning American values of freedom and democracy.

source_summaries.title: AVDD Strait of Hormuz SITREP
bullets: Economic coercion and control of maritime access increasingly define the regional crisis, with commercial traffic in the Strait of Hormuz remaining low while substantial oil volumes move through the Omani route.

Iran retains its capability to target shipping and U.S.-Gulf allies to preserve maritime leverage, although domestic political pressures and deteriorating economic conditions are driving some internal debate over ending the conflict.
Houthi pressure on Saudi shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb is disrupting regional energy flows, prompting Riyadh to adopt alternative shipping and pipeline arrangements.

source_summaries.title: Debt and Tax Cuts
bullets: Federal debt has grown very large, with total figures reaching historic highs relative to the economy.
While some attribute the debt growth to public spending or aging populations, the primary driver is revenue loss from tax cuts enacted by Republican presidents.
Tax cuts implemented under George W. Bush and Donald Trump are identified as the core reason U.S. debt is currently so high as a percentage of GDP.

source_summaries.title: Sunday thought: We!
bullets: State Representative Angie Nixon won Florida's Democratic primary for a U.S. Senate seat against a heavily funded opponent, reflecting a broader trend of progressive primary upsets.
Progressive candidates across the country are succeeding by focusing on key economic concerns like healthcare, childcare, and anti-corruption despite facing long odds and well-funded opponents.
A growing grassroots movement and widespread public backlash against the current presidential administration are fueling a new wave of progressive political engagement.

source_summaries.title: Weekend Update #199: Ukraine’s Campaign Against Russian Oil Infrastructure Should Be The Focus
bullets: Ukraine should continuously focus its airpower on dismantling Russia's fuel system rather than targeting infrastructure like Wildberries that lacks equivalent strategic warfighting impact.
Recent evidence highlights the extreme vulnerability of Russia's oil refineries, pipelines, and shipping to targeted attacks.
Reports emerged indicating that former President Trump blocked Starlink from assisting Ukraine.

source_summaries.source: Heather Cox Richardson from Letters from an American
source_summaries.title: August 22, 2026
bullets: During a South Carolina Republican senatorial primary debate, Senator Darline Graham admitted she was not well-informed on national security when asked about Taiwan and the South China Sea.
Appearing on Fox News following the debate, Graham defended her comment by claiming it showed she is not a politician and pivoted to standard Republican culture war talking points.
Appointed to the Senate to fill a vacancy, Graham relies on her loyalty to Donald Trump and echoes his platform, though Trump's backed candidates have recently faced multiple primary losses.

source_summaries.title: 🔮 Why one AI is better than four #598
bullets: Anthropic experiments show that a single AI agent evaluates evidence and makes correct decisions more reliably than a group of four interacting agents suffering from groupthink.
LLM multi-agent systems struggle because models lack output diversity and lack the institutional safeguards that protect human dissenters.
Token price elasticity for AI remains underwhelming because users and firms struggle to properly define and price a useful unit of knowledge work.

publications: Heather Cox Richardson from Letters from an American
